extra.message: projectVendorCommissionScenario builds a JS function from the user-controlled `formula` query parameter (`const projector = new Function('inputs', \`with (inputs) { return (${formula}); }\`)`) and executes it server-side. Any authenticated vendor_manager/marketplace_admin can reach GET /:id/commission-scenario and achieve arbitrary code execution (RCE) in the Node process. The '/verified' twin endpoint (line 1061) correctly restricts input to an allowlist of scenario functions.

generateVendorStatementDocument concatenates the unvalidated `outputFormat` request body field into a shell command and executes it via `spawn('bash', ['-c', convertCmd], { shell: true })`. An authenticated vendor_manager (no vendor ownership check is performed either) can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g. outputFormat = 'pdf && curl ...') leading to remote code execution. Contrast with generateDisputeCaseArchive (line 240), which uses a format allowlist and argument-array spawn.

searchProductsByMerchandisingFilter interpolates the `categoryName` and `keyword` query parameters directly into a raw SQL string executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe (`AND c.name = '${categoryName}'` / `AND p.name ILIKE '%${keyword}%'`). This is classic SQL injection (single-quote breakout) allowing data exfiltration / tampering.

applyCarrierIntegrationProfile passes the attacker-controlled `x-custom-config` XML header to readCarrierProfile (PUT /:id/carrier-profile). carrierProfileReader.expandGeneralEntities (utils/carrierProfileReader.ts:9-27) resolves `<!ENTITY name SYSTEM "path">` declarations with fs.readFileSync(systemLiteral), so an XML payload such as `<!ENTITY f SYSTEM "/etc/passwd"><notes>&f;</notes>` causes arbitrary local file contents to be embedded in the returned profile JSON — a local file disclosure (XXE). The strict variant readCarrierProfileStrict (used by the /preview endpoint) rejects DOCTYPE, confirming the issue.

fetchComplianceDocument joins the raw `req.params.docName` into a filesystem path (`path.join(complianceDocsDir, req.params.docName)`) with no basename/sandbox check before streaming the file to the client. A vendor owner/admin can request GET /:id/compliance-docs/..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd to read arbitrary server files. The '/verified' twin (line 1008) applies path.basename(), confirming the traversal.

cacheVendorReturnPolicyDraft interpolates the unvalidated `x-policy-locale` request header into a file path (`path.join(returnPolicyDraftsDir, \`${vendor.id}-${locale}.html\`)`) and writes attacker-controlled content there (fs.writeFileSync). A locale such as `..%2f..%2f..%2ftmp%2fx` lets an owner/admin write files outside the drafts directory — path traversal write primitive (limited to the `.html` suffix on the final segment).

previewExternalCatalogFeed performs a server-side fetch() of the URL supplied in the `x-catalog-feed-url` request header with no allowlist/validation, returning up to 2000 bytes of the response body. An authenticated vendor owner/admin can probe internal network resources (SSRF), e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or internal services. The '/verified' twin (line 1156) restricts hosts via ALLOWED_CATALOG_FEED_HOSTS.

renderVendorStorefrontWidget interpolates vendor-controlled fields (vendor.name, vendor.description, latestReview.title/body) into an HTML page sent as text/html with no escaping, despite escapeHtml() being imported and unused in this file. A vendor can store `<script>` markup in their name/description/review which executes in the browser of any authenticated user viewing GET /:slug/widget — stored XSS.

renderProductComparisonWidget reflects the raw `x-compare-label` request header into an inline <script> (`var kmCompareLabel = "${compareLabel}"`) without escaping, so a value like `"; alert(document.cookie); "` breaks out of the JS string and executes in the response origin — reflected XSS (compare with renderCategoryPromoWidget in products.ts:293 which escapes via escapeHtml).

syncAccountPreferences (PATCH /api/users/me/preferences, any authenticated user) spreads the entire request body over the full user record and writes it straight to prisma.user.update, deleting only `id` and `passwordHash`. A buyer can set `role: "marketplace_admin"` (and isActive/emailVerified/etc.) to escalate privileges to a marketplace admin — mass-assignment privilege escalation. No field allowlist is applied.

searchStaffEscalationRoster builds an LDAP filter by concatenating the `escalationDeskUnit` cookie and the `q` query parameter with no escaping (`(&(department=${deskUnit})(cn=*${q}*))`), then passes it to directoryClient.search. Metacharacters such as `)`/`*` let an attacker alter filter logic to enumerate directory entries beyond the intended department. The adjacent verifyDeskGroupMembership (line 253) escapes inputs with escapeDirectoryFilterValue(), demonstrating the missing control.

viewProductSourcingDetails (GET /:id/sourcing-details) is mounted on the public /api/products router and has no authentication. Access to the vendor's payoutEmail, taxId and the product moderationNote is gated only by the client-supplied `membershipStatus` value in the query/body — any anonymous caller can send membershipStatus=wholesale_partner and read sensitive vendor financial data for any product. The '/verified' twin (line 406) requires authenticate + owner/admin role checks.

resolveCarrierHandoffLink verifies the carrier link JWT with `algorithms: ['HS256', 'none']` and, if verification throws, falls back to unsigned `jwt.decode(link)` (line 350). The signature is therefore never enforced: any authenticated user can craft a token with alg:none (or an unsigned payload) containing an arbitrary `orderId` and read that order's shippingName, shippingAddress and trackingNumber via GET /carrier-handoff/:link — broken access control / signature bypass on other users' PII.

extra.message: lookupShipmentTrackingByCookie interpolates the attacker-controlled `trackingRef` cookie directly into an XPath expression passed to queryShipmentDocument. Because the endpoint first indexes ALL orders (including shippingAddress as internalNotes) with no per-user scoping, an injection such as `x' or '1'='1` returns shipment records for every order — exposing other customers' tracking numbers and shipping addresses (XPath injection). The '/verified' warranty endpoint (line 463) uses escapeXPathString().

relayCarrierManifestUpdate (POST /:id/carrier-manifest) applies no ownership or role check — any authenticated user (e.g. a buyer) can update the trackingNumber and notes of ANY order by id. Combined with the hardcoded AES fallback key on line 16, arbitrary order records can be tampered with. Compare with the ownership checks present on every other order mutation in this file.

extra.message: renderOrderReceipt builds the template path from the user-controlled `template` query parameter via path.join(receiptTemplatesDir, `${template}.html`) with no allowlist or sandbox check. A `template` of `../../../path/to/file` lets an authorized order viewer read arbitrary `.html` files from the server filesystem through the receipt endpoint.

attachDisputeEvidenceFile concatenates the fully user-controlled `filename` body field with the dispute id and writes base64-decoded content to disk (fs.writeFileSync(path.join(evidenceDir, `${dispute.id}-${filename}`))) with no basename/allowlist. A filename of `../../../../tmp/evil` writes attacker-controlled bytes outside the evidence directory — path traversal write (CWE-22).

applyCarrierEscalationBridge authorizes a privileged dispute mutation purely from the spoofable request headers `x-carrier-desk-role` and `x-carrier-desk-tier` (no API-key/role verification — authenticateApiKey passes through when no key header is present) and then spreads the entire attacker-controlled `req.body.updates` object into prisma.dispute.update. Any authenticated low-privilege user can claim trusted_partner and rewrite arbitrary fields (status, resolution, refundAmount) of ANY dispute. The '/verified' twin (line 688) restricts updates to an allowlist.

extra.message: syncCaseWorkspaceNotes uses the support/admin-set `workspaceFolder` (saved verbatim from request body in setCaseWorkspacePreference) directly in path.join(caseWorkspaceRoot, workspaceFolder, `${dispute.id}.txt`) with no containment check, allowing read/write of arbitrary `.txt` files outside the workspace root. The '/verified' twin (line 617) resolves and validates the prefix.

resumeStorefrontSetupDraft JSON-parses the attacker-controlled `storefrontSetupDraft` cookie and spreads the entire object into prisma.vendor.update data with no field validation. A vendor can bake fields such as `status: "active"` or `verifiedAt` into the cookie to self-approve/self-verify their own vendor record, bypassing the admin-only status transition logic. The '/verified' twin (line 895) validates against a zod schema.

resumeUnfinishedReviewDraft parses the attacker-controlled `reviewComposerDraft` cookie and spreads it wholesale into prisma.review.update. A review author can set fields they must not control (status, moderationNote, response/respondedAt, productId/vendorId, etc.), bypassing the field-level checks used in PATCH /:id. The '/verified' twin (line 239) validates with a zod schema restricted to rating/title/body.

applyBulkListingUpdate (POST /listing-patch) parses the raw `listingPatch` form field as JSON and passes it directly as prisma.product.update data with no schema filtering. A vendor_manager can set `status: "published"` to publish their own products without admin review (the products.ts PATCH endpoint explicitly forbids vendors from publishing, allowing only draft/pending_review/archived), plus modify price/inventory arbitrarily. The '/verified' twin (line 254) validates with listingPatchSchema.

confirmWebhookTestDelivery redirects to the unvalidated `x-return-to` request header value (res.redirect(returnTo)). Because the route is a GET (no CSRF token, no body), an attacker who can influence the header on a victim request can redirect the authenticated webhook owner to an arbitrary external site (open redirect / phishing). The '/verified' twin (line 172) restricts destinations with an allowlist.

submitComplianceIntake logs the entire request body — including `taxId` and `bankRoutingNumber` — to stdout via console.log (JSON.stringify(req.body)), exposing sensitive financial data in application logs (CWE-532). Note importVendorBankingCredentials elsewhere encrypts such fields with sealVendorKycField before storage.

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to the hardcoded value 'local-dev-secret' when JWT_SECRET is unset (also duplicated in vendors.ts:18). An attacker who knows the default can forge valid auth tokens for any user (including marketplace_admin) and forge partnership/teammate grants and carrier-handoff links.

CARRIER_HANDOFF_SECRET and the AES-256-CBC manifest key both fall back to hardcoded values ('local-dev-secret' / 'local-manifest-key'). Anyone knowing these defaults can forge valid carrier handoff/return-pickup links (data disclosure) and forge encrypted carrier-manifest payloads to alter arbitrary order tracking fields.

initiateInstantDisbursement uses a hardcoded live-looking ledger API key fallback (`'lk_live_9f3a2c7d4e1b8f60a3d92e77c41f0a5b'`) when LEDGER_API_KEY is unset, and the payout-instruction encryption key falls back to 'local-payout-key' (line 11). These hardcoded credentials would allow forging/decrypting payout instruction updates.

generateApiKey derives API key prefixes/secrets from Math.random() (Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length)), a non-cryptographic PRNG. API keys are security credentials and must be generated with crypto.randomBytes / randomUUID; Math.random-based keys are predictable and brute-forceable.

extra.message: inspectShipmentSyncFailure returns the raw exception message, stack trace and order shippingAddress/trackingNumber in a 500 response whenever `?context=verbose` is supplied. This discloses internal server details (CWE-209) and the full shipping address of the order to any participant who is otherwise authorized to view it but should not see server stack internals.

extra.message: notifyVendorDisputeOutcome places the webhook signing secret into the outbound URL query string (`${webhook.url}?event=...&signing_key=${encodeURIComponent(webhook.secret)}`). Secrets in URLs can be leaked via HTTP(S) request logs, proxies and the vendor's own access logs (CWE-598/200).

extra.message: registerDisbursementPasscode uses the client-supplied numeric `securityLevel` directly as the bcrypt cost factor (`bcrypt.hash(passcode, tier)`). A large cost (e.g. 31) makes bcryptjs hash synchronously for an extremely long time, blocking Node's event loop (DoS, CWE-400); a tiny cost (0/1) produces trivially weak hashes.
